questions.question: Boot-shaped country that invented pizza and takes pineapple on it as a personal insult.
questions.bonus: Say "Ciao!" with the full Italian hand gesture

questions.question: Country that is mostly kangaroos, sunburn and things that want to bite you. Locals call it "Straya".
questions.bonus: Say "G'day, mate!" like a real Aussie

questions.question: Country where dinner starts at 10 pm, everyone naps after lunch, and once a year a whole town throws tomatoes at each other on purpose.
questions.bonus: Say "¡Hola!" and do a 3-second flamenco stomp
questions.funFact: The tomato fight is La Tomatina, held every August in the town of Buñol.

questions.question: Country famous for chocolate, fancy watches, cheese with holes, and being extremely neutral about everything.
questions.bonus: Say "Grüezi!" (Swiss-German hello) and yodel for 3 seconds

questions.question: Land of volcanoes and glaciers, where the phone book is sorted by first name because surnames are just "son of" or "daughter of" your dad.
questions.bonus: Say "Halló!" and do the Viking thunder-clap: arms up, "HUH!"

categories.name: Flags in Emoji
categories.note: Guess the country from its flag 🏳️

questions.bonus: Say "Konnichiwa" with a polite bow
questions.funFact: The flag is called Hinomaru, the "circle of the sun".

questions.bonus: Say "Hello, bonjour!" and apologise to someone for no reason
questions.funFact: The maple leaf flag only became Canada's flag in 1965.

questions.question: ⬛ on top, 🟥 in the middle, 🟨 at the bottom
questions.bonus: Say "Guten Tag!" like a very serious train announcer

questions.question: 🟩🔶🔵⭐ (green, a yellow diamond, a starry blue globe)
questions.bonus: Say "Olá!" and samba for 3 seconds
questions.funFact: The stars show the sky over Rio de Janeiro on the morning of 15 November 1889.

questions.question: 🟦 + 🇬🇧 in the corner + four ⭐ (red ones!)
questions.bonus: Say "Kia ora!" (Māori hello) and wave like a hobbit

questions.question: Big metal tower in Paris. Climbed some of it. Legs gone. Croissant was nice.
questions.bonus: Say "Bonjour!" in your most dramatic French accent
questions.funFact: It was built for the 1889 World's Fair and was meant to be temporary.

questions.question: Huge white marble building in Agra. Woke up at 5 am for the sunrise photo. So did four thousand other people.
questions.bonus: Say "Namaste!" and do the pinch-the-dome photo pose

questions.question: Very long wall. Walked for 20 minutes. Saw maybe 0.01% of it. Apparently not even visible from space.
questions.bonus: Say "Nǐ hǎo!" and march along an imaginary wall
questions.funFact: Despite the famous myth, you can't see it from space with the naked eye.

questions.question: Ancient stone city way up in the Andes mountains. Train, then bus, then a llama photobombed me.
questions.bonus: Say "¡Hola!" and pose for a selfie with an imaginary llama

questions.question: Giant stone heads on a tiny island in the middle of the Pacific. Nobody would tell me how they moved them.
questions.bonus: Make your most serious stone-head face for 5 seconds
questions.funFact: The statues are called moai, and many have bodies buried underground.

questions.question: Flat round bread, tomato sauce and melted cheese, cut into triangles, delivered in a box bigger than itself.
questions.bonus: Say "Mamma mia!" with the pinched-fingers gesture

questions.question: Raw fish placed lovingly on vinegared rice, sometimes wrapped in seaweed, eaten with a dab of green fire.
questions.bonus: Say "Itadakimasu!" and eat imaginary sushi with imaginary chopsticks

questions.question: Folded Mexican tortilla that collapses the second you bite it, sending the fillings straight onto your shirt.
questions.bonus: Say "¡Hola!" and eat an imaginary taco without spilling

questions.question: Ground chickpeas rolled into little balls, deep-fried, and stuffed into pita bread.
questions.bonus: Say "Marhaba!" (Arabic hello) with a big smile

questions.question: Scottish dish: a sheep's heart, liver and lungs, minced with oats and cooked inside the sheep's stomach. Served with a poem.
questions.bonus: Say "Hello!" in your best Scottish accent
questions.funFact: Scots eat it on Burns Night, when Robert Burns's poem "Address to a Haggis" is read aloud.

questions.question: Real or made up: Scotland's national animal is the unicorn.
questions.bonus: Gallop like a unicorn and say hello in a Scottish accent

questions.question: Real or made up: In 1932, Australia sent soldiers to fight a "war" against emus, and the emus won.
questions.bonus: Run around like an emu that just won a war

questions.question: Real or made up: Canada keeps an emergency strategic reserve of maple syrup.
questions.bonus: Say "Hello, eh!" and pour imaginary syrup on everything nearby
questions.funFact: Quebec's maple syrup producers keep millions of pounds of it in warehouses.

questions.question: Real or made up: It's against the law to die inside the Houses of Parliament in London.
questions.bonus: Say "Good evening" like a very posh British butler

questions.question: Real or made up: There's a village in Norway called Hell, and it freezes over every winter.
questions.bonus: Say "Hei!" (Norwegian hello) with chattering teeth

categories.name: Overly Wordy History
categories.note: Read it like a very serious documentary 🎙️

questions.question: A large and allegedly unsinkable British passenger vessel which, on its very first voyage in 1912, had an unscheduled and deeply regrettable meeting with an iceberg.
questions.bonus: Do the "I'm flying" pose at the front of an imaginary ship

questions.question: In 1969, two gentlemen took an extremely long road trip, parked on a large grey rock, walked around in bulky outfits, and left behind a flag and some footprints.
questions.bonus: Take "one small step" in super slow motion

questions.question: A wall built in 1961 to keep a city's own residents in, which those same residents enthusiastically took apart with hammers in 1989.
questions.bonus: Say "Hallo!" and knock down an imaginary wall

questions.question: In 1773, some colonists upset about a tax disguised themselves and threw 342 chests of perfectly good tea into a harbour. Every desi watching is still upset.
questions.bonus: Mourn the lost tea by sipping an imaginary cup of chai, very sadly

questions.question: A famous 1930 walk of about 240 miles to the sea, which ended with one man picking up a handful of salt and shaking an entire empire.
questions.bonus: Walk to the "sea" in slow motion and pick up imaginary salt
questions.funFact: Gandhi set out from Sabarmati Ashram with 78 marchers, and it took 24 days.

questions.question: Glass rectangle you stare at for seven hours a day which, technically, can also make phone calls.
questions.bonus: Act out your phone dying at 1%

questions.question: A tiny wooden stick with a controlled explosion on one end.
questions.bonus: Light an imaginary matchstick first try, then blow it out dramatically

questions.question: A bent piece of wire that holds paper together, and was once Microsoft's most annoying assistant.
questions.bonus: Say "It looks like you're writing a letter!" in a cheerful robot voice

questions.question: Invented after an engineer working on radar noticed the chocolate bar in his pocket had melted.
questions.bonus: Count down the last 3 seconds before an imaginary microwave beeps
questions.funFact: The engineer was Percy Spencer, and the first one was nearly as tall as a fridge.

questions.question: A glue so weak it was considered a failure, until someone used it to stop bookmarks falling out of his choir hymn book.
questions.bonus: Stick an imaginary note on a teammate's forehead and read it out
questions.funFact: Spencer Silver invented the glue; his colleague Art Fry came up with the bookmark idea.

questions.question: Real or made up: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.
questions.bonus: Pose like a pharaoh for 5 seconds
questions.funFact: The Great Pyramid is about 2,500 years older than Cleopatra.

questions.question: Real or made up: Vikings wore horned helmets into battle.
questions.bonus: Do a Viking roar (no horns allowed)
questions.funFact: The horns came from 1800s costume designers, especially for Wagner's operas.

questions.question: Real or made up: Napoleon was unusually short.
questions.answer: Made up (he was about average height)
questions.bonus: Strike the Napoleon pose: one hand tucked inside your jacket

questions.question: Real or made up: Oxford University is older than the Aztec Empire.
questions.bonus: Say "Good afternoon" like a very posh Oxford professor
questions.funFact: Teaching at Oxford began around 1096; the Aztec capital was founded in 1325.

questions.question: Real or made up: In 1919, a giant wave of molasses swept through the streets of Boston.
questions.bonus: Move in slow motion as if wading through syrup
questions.funFact: The wave was several metres high and moved at around 35 mph.

questions.question: "I have a dream"
questions.bonus: Say "Hello" in your most inspiring speech voice

questions.question: "Veni, vidi, vici" (I came, I saw, I conquered)
questions.bonus: Say "Salve!" (Latin hello) and conquer the snack table

questions.question: "Be the change you wish to see in the world" (famously credited to him, though he never put it quite like that)
questions.bonus: Say "Namaste" with the calmest smile you have
questions.funFact: Those exact words aren't in his writings; it's a short version of a longer idea of his.

questions.question: "Let them eat cake" (the queen famously blamed for it, who almost certainly never said it)
questions.bonus: Say "Bonjour!" and offer everyone imaginary cake
questions.funFact: The line appears in Rousseau's writing from when she was still a child.

questions.question: "Mr. Watson, come here, I want to see you" (the first words ever spoken over a telephone)
questions.bonus: Answer an imaginary telephone the way he wanted everyone to: "Ahoy!"
questions.funFact: Bell wanted people to answer the phone with "Ahoy!" instead of "Hello".

questions.question: Giant triangle-shaped tomb in the Egyptian desert. Thousands of years old. Still no lift.
questions.bonus: Walk like an Egyptian for 5 seconds

questions.question: Huge stone arena in Rome where crowds watched gladiators. Basically a stadium with fewer snacks.
questions.bonus: Give a dramatic Roman-emperor thumbs up or down and say "Ciao!"

questions.question: A ring of enormous stones standing in an English field. Nobody is sure why. Still an excellent selfie spot.
questions.bonus: Stand perfectly still like a giant stone for 5 seconds

questions.question: Mayan pyramid in Mexico where, on the spring equinox, shadows make a snake appear to slither down the steps.
questions.bonus: Slither down an imaginary staircase like the shadow snake

questions.question: Cambodian temple, the largest religious monument on Earth, so important it appears on the country's national flag.
questions.bonus: Greet everyone with palms pressed together, Cambodian-style
